question: Can trained hidden features escape the small-SiLU even-channel bottleneck?

architecture.parameterization: z=scale*x*W/sqrt(dim), W initialized N(0,1); scale stays fixed
architecture.normalization: subtract initial train feature mean and divide fixed initial total RMS, then sqrt(width)

predictions.claim: On symmetric data at0.03 SiLU has weaker interaction progress than ReLU, while its linear progress is not weaker, in both frozen/learned modes at step1.
predictions.criterion: interaction initial progress ratio<0.1; linear ratio>0.5; allseeds
predictions.scope: head initialized zero, hidden initial gradient exactly zero

predictions.claim: At0.03 on symmetric data, learned hidden improves SiLU interaction train MSE by step1024 versus frozen in at least3/4seeds, but does not universally remove slowdown versus ReLU.
predictions.criterion: learned wins>=3; atstep128 median SiLU train MSE exceeds ReLU

predictions.claim: The initial frozen-spectrum train curve ceases to predict full-hidden training, whereas it predicts frozen mode.
predictions.scope: negative test of fixed-feature theory outside assumptions

predictions.claim: Learned-hidden escape from the interaction bottleneck is accompanied by growth of centered even feature energy or changed target-aligned kernel energy.
predictions.criterion: SiLU learned interaction: at leastone of final/initial even energy or kernel energy exceeds1.2 in>=3/4seeds
predictions.scope: symmetric0.03; correlation diagnostic, not mediation proof

statistical_unit: two target/distribution recipes, four within-condition seeds
